title: UEFI Variable Storage
description: Stores boot configuration in UEFI NVRAM variables with authenticated write support. BootOrder, keys, and settings persist across power loss; authenticated variables need signed updates. It is the firmware's key-value store.

demo.title: Demo — UEFI Variable Storage

title: Battery-Backed SRAM
description: Keeps SRAM alive with a battery so state survives power loss with SRAM speed. Write latency is nanoseconds and endurance is unlimited; the battery needs monitoring. Industrial controllers rely on it.

demo.title: Demo — Battery-Backed SRAM

title: MRAM and FRAM
description: Uses magnetoresistive and ferroelectric RAM for byte-addressable non-volatility. No battery, no wear leveling, instant writes — the ideal NVRAM technologies maturing now. They replace battery-backed SRAM in new designs.

demo.title: Demo — MRAM and FRAM

title: Persistent Memory (PMEM)
description: Maps persistent memory into the address space for DAX-speed durable storage. Loads and stores are durable; no page cache or block layer in the way. It blurs the line between memory and storage.

demo.title: Demo — Persistent Memory (PMEM)

title: DAX Filesystems
description: Builds filesystems with direct access to persistent memory, bypassing the page cache. Reads and writes hit the media directly at memory speed. It is the filesystem for the PMEM era.

demo.title: Demo — DAX Filesystems

title: Wear Leveling
description: Spreads writes evenly across flash cells so no block wears out early. The FTL remaps logical addresses to the least-worn physical blocks; static data gets rotated too. It multiplies flash lifespan.

demo.title: Demo — Wear Leveling

title: Atomic Journaled Writes
description: Journals NVRAM writes so power loss never leaves half-written state. The journal records intent, the write commits, then the journal clears; recovery replays incomplete journals. Atomicity from ordering.

demo.title: Demo — Atomic Journaled Writes

title: Power-Fail Safety
description: Guarantees in-flight writes complete on power loss with hold-up capacitors. Voltage monitors trigger an emergency flush using stored energy; the window is milliseconds but enough. Enterprise SSDs all do this.

demo.title: Demo — Power-Fail Safety

title: Secure NVRAM with TPM
description: Seals NVRAM secrets to TPM PCRs so they only unseal on trusted boot. Disk encryption keys live in sealed NVRAM; a tampered boot cannot unseal them. It binds secrets to system integrity.

demo.title: Demo — Secure NVRAM with TPM

title: RTC CMOS Storage
description: Keeps clock and BIOS settings in battery-backed CMOS. Tiny capacity but always there; the classic PC NVRAM. Modern systems moved most settings to flash, but the RTC endures.

demo.title: Demo — RTC CMOS Storage

title: SPI Flash Layout
description: Lays out firmware, settings, and recovery images in SPI flash regions. Protected regions guard the boot block; the layout is documented for recovery tools. It is the map of the firmware world.

demo.title: Demo — SPI Flash Layout

title: NVDIMM Persistence
description: Uses NVDIMM-N modules that copy DRAM to flash on power loss. Full DRAM speed while powered, flash durability when not; the supercapacitor powers the save. It is DRAM that survives outages.

demo.title: Demo — NVDIMM Persistence

title: Persistence Barriers
description: Orders persistent writes with cache-line write-back and fences. clwb pushes lines to the persistence domain; sfence orders them. Without barriers, durable does not mean ordered.

demo.title: Demo — Persistence Barriers

title: Checksum Protection
description: Protects NVRAM contents with CRCs so corruption is detected, not trusted. Every structure carries a checksum verified on read; mismatches trigger recovery. Silent corruption is the enemy.

demo.title: Demo — Checksum Protection

title: NVRAM Recovery Procedures
description: Defines recovery when NVRAM is corrupt: defaults, backups, and factory images. The procedure is tested, not improvised; last-known-good copies are kept. Recovery is a plan, not a hope.

demo.title: Demo — NVRAM Recovery Procedures
